# CVG

Two-table vine-copula synthetic data generator and evaluation framework.

## Setup

### Prerequisites

- Python 3.12+
- [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) — fast Python package and project manager

### Install uv

```bash
curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh
```

### Create environment and install dependencies

```bash
uv sync
```

This creates a `.venv` virtual environment and installs all project dependencies.

### Install dev dependencies (Jupyter support)

```bash
uv sync --group dev
```

### Use the package in Jupyter

```bash
uv pip install -e .
```

## Walk-through: UCI Online Retail

End-to-end example — download the UCI Online Retail dataset, prepare it into
the two-table parent/child layout, fit the generator, and produce a synthetic
copy.

### 1. Download the raw data

```bash
uv run python scripts/download_data.py
```

Fetches a public datasets bundle (~8 MB compressed) from Google Drive and
extracts it into `data/raw/`:

- `data/raw/uci_retail/online_retail.csv` — raw UCI Online Retail (id 352)
- `data/raw/rossmann/historical.csv`, `data/raw/rossmann/store.csv` —
  SyntheRela Rossmann subsample (2014-07-31 .. 2014-09-30)

The Drive file ID is hardcoded in `scripts/download_data.py` — change
`DRIVE_FILE_ID` there if you mirror the bundle elsewhere.

### 2. Prepare the relational tables

```bash
uv run python src/prepare_data_uci.py \
    --input data/raw/uci_retail/online_retail.csv \
    --output-dir data/prepared/uci
```

Produces in `data/prepared/uci/`:

- `customers.csv` — parent table (one row per customer)
- `purchases.csv` — child table (one row per invoice)
- `metadata.yml`, `prep_report.txt` — provenance for this prep run

### 3. Fit the generator

```bash
uv run python src/fit_generator_v1.py \
    --data-dir data/prepared/uci \
    --metadata configs/uci_online_retail_generator_v1.yaml \
    --output-dir artifacts/uci
```

Writes fitted artifacts (K-means, parent vine, per-cluster child vines, and
an `artifact_manifest.yml`) to `artifacts/uci/`.

### 4. Generate synthetic data

```bash
uv run python src/generate_data_v1.py \
    --artifacts-dir artifacts/uci \
    --real-data-dir data/prepared/uci \
    --output-dir data/synthetic/uci \
    --scale 1.0
```

Writes `synthetic_customers.csv` and `synthetic_purchases.csv` to
`data/synthetic/uci/`. Use `--scale` to produce a sample sized as a fraction
of the real parent table, or `--n-parent N` to request an exact parent
row count. `--random-state` controls reproducibility.

### 5. Evaluate the synthetic data

```bash
uv run python src/evaluate_method.py \
    --real-data-dir data/prepared/uci \
    --metadata configs/uci_online_retail_evaluator.yaml \
    --synthetic-dir data/synthetic/uci \
    --method-name v1 \
    --output-dir experiments/uci/v1
```

Compares the synthetic tables in `--synthetic-dir` against the real tables
in `--real-data-dir` and writes the Level 1/2/3 fidelity metrics
(marginals, correlations, tail dependence, relational consistency) plus
plots and a Markdown report into `--output-dir`. `--method-name` is just a
label that propagates into the report and the per-method CSV filenames so
multiple methods can be aggregated downstream.

Note that step 5 uses a different metadata file (`*_evaluator.yaml`) than
step 3 (`*_generator_v1.yaml`): the evaluator config declares column roles,
tail-dependence pairs, and aggregate-consistency targets, while the
generator config declares the modelled-column list and per-column
constraints/transforms.
